name: Lasombra Institutions: Courts of Blood (Clanbook: Lasombra)

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("The Keepers' Unlit Halls").

Long before the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} existed, the Lasombra Antediluvian recognized that its childer would prey upon one another and set up the Courts of Blood so that such predation could be bound by rules — the destruction of a clanmate made a reward granted through procedure and policy rather than mere opportunism. The Courts predate the Sabbat itself, having moved with Roman-era Lasombra away from older Babylonian antecedents, and they continued to function even through the chaos of the Antediluvian's destruction and the founding of the sect. In the era before organized @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} governance in the New World, the Courts of Blood were, for several decades, the closest thing to procedural justice on that continent, and the Friends of the Night even contracted out the courts' services to Camarilla Kindred seeking disputes settled — a fact none of the surviving participants care to admit.

Procedure: A Lasombra with a grievance against a clanmate begins by making her dissatisfaction known, speaking to the powerful Lasombra in her vicinity. They confer among themselves, and anywhere from three to 13 members of the Friends of the Night convene as a Court of Blood. The court hears the plaintiff's petition, then dismisses her while it deliberates — deliberation can take minutes or years, and while it continues, the plaintiff must not press her case further or risk destruction herself for impatience or presumption.

Outcomes: In over half of all cases, the court rules the complaint has insufficient merit; the plaintiff is reprimanded for poor judgment and sometimes sanctioned (such as loss of Status). In roughly 10–15% of cases, the court orders the target to suffer some punishment short of destruction: surrendering information or assets, or granting the plaintiff certain property or influence taken from the target. In the remaining cases, the court agrees the target warrants destruction, often bound by constraints (no use of Disciplines, destruction of the target's ghouls and possessions before the target itself, etc.). One or more Lasombra must witness the act of destruction to confirm it was carried out as ordered.

Anonymity and appeal: The court convenes in darkness. The plaintiff should not know which local clanmates sit in judgment — she is summoned anonymously to a meeting place and finds the judges already cloaked by Obtenebration, Obfuscate, or other concealment. No formal procedure for appeal exists. Attempting to destroy another Lasombra (other than an antitribu) without court sanction is itself grounds for a complaint before the court.

MET/Storyteller note: The Courts of Blood make an excellent plot engine for Lasombra-heavy chronicles — a way to formalize intra-clan conflict resolution, extract a price from a rival short of Final Death, or threaten a PC with anonymous judgment. Storytellers may run a Court as a scene with hidden NPC judges (or player-judges under domino masks/Obtenebration effects) to preserve the anonymity the institution depends on.

Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two — the elder Demba's counsel to her fledgling Ming on approaching the Courts of Blood.

  • Be prepared in advance. Document your grievances plausibly before you ever bring them forward; a petition built on rumor alone invites the reprimand reserved for poor judgment.
  • Be concise. The Friends of the Night have little patience for rambling plaintiffs.
  • Offer kickbacks and incentives — carefully. Sweeteners can help your case, but never assume you know who is or isn't sitting in judgment; an insult aimed at an unseen judge can doom the petition.
  • Be respectful and confident. Neither groveling nor arrogance serves a petitioner well before the court.
  • Follow all instructions the court gives, completely. Partial compliance with a court's ruling is treated as no compliance at all.
  • Do not get greedy. Petitioning too often draws skeptical attention and marks a Lasombra as a nuisance or a schemer rather than a Kindred with genuine grievances.

MET/Storyteller note: This list doubles as a practical checklist for players roleplaying a Lasombra character bringing a plot device (a rival's transgression, a stolen asset, a broken oath) before an in-game Court of Blood, and as a rubric a Storyteller running the court scene can use to reward or penalize a petitioner's roleplaying.

Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, Chapter Two ("The Keepers' Unlit Halls").

Behind the Courts of Blood stand the Friends of the Night, a loose-knit network of clan elders and a select few younger members who have proven themselves exceptionally capable. Like the courts, the Friends predate all known civilizations, and their name is rendered in whatever language most firmly signals culture and authority to those who hear it — "Brether Nokw," "Amici Noctis," "Les amis noirs," and now, commonly, "Friends of the Night." Members take a simple oath to protect the interests of the clan as a whole and to work against its enemies.

Most Lasombra who survive a century or so of unlife receive an invitation to join the Friends, nominated by an existing Friend after consultation among the membership, typically following some remarkable feat. The Friends of the Night are the only clanwide institution the Lasombra maintain — consensus within the clan holds that overly rigid structures inevitably turn on their creators, so everything else about Lasombra organization operates flexibly and with substantial local autonomy.

It was the Friends of the Night, convened as the Amici Noctis, whom Gratiano de Veronese confronted immediately after destroying the Lasombra Antediluvian in 1483 — presenting them with the deed already done and daring them to condemn him. The Friends listened, stepped aside, and let events unfold; some joined Gratiano's revolt outright, others held back, but none moved to oppose him. It was likewise at Gratiano's urging that the Friends declined ever after to anoint a successor to the Antediluvian's throne, leaving every Lasombra to decide for themselves what the clan lineage means.
